findings.title: Missing Schema.org Organization structured data on root landing page
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://www.aa.com/ via jsonld_schema_extractor [2026-09-13T17:48:14Z]: Root homepage contains 0 Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema blocks. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (citation-simulator): Observed at https://www.aa.com/ via onsite_answerability_probe [2026-09-13T17:48:14Z]: Across 1 crawled page(s), no Organization/LocalBusiness schema states who the brand is in machine-readable form. An assistant that fetched these pages could not quote an answer to "What is Aa?" from this site, so it must fall back to third-party sources or omit the brand. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add Organization JSON-LD markup to the homepage.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a JSON-LD script on the homepage declaring @type 'Organization' with name, url, logo, and sameAs links to authoritative profiles.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves structured data by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

proactive_recommendations.title: Build third-party presence so Aa is resolvable away from its own domain
proactive_recommendations.rationale: Only 0 independent authority domain(s) are referenced from the crawled pages. A brand described only on its own site is a single fragile source no matter how well that site is built.

WebSite ties the domain to the brand entity and, with a potentialAction SearchAction, lets assistants point users straight into your own search instead of guessing at URLs. proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.

Be aware this is a low-evidence convention rather than an established standard: 2026 measurements find major AI crawlers almost never request the file, and Google has stated it has no effect on Search or AI Overviews. It costs very little to publish and may matter if uptake improves, but it should be treated as optionality -- not as a substitute for the structured data and third-party presence that demonstrably drive citation today.
